decisions.reason: The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY for the separate underside maintenance-access clause. Sanitation access for liquid-contact parts does not change its maintenance and service criteria.
The sanitation-access requirement does not select, replace, or otherwise change any BOM component or component-selection obligation.
The whisk already must detach for cleaning, and the general sanitation-access decision does not change its configuration, attachment, or cleaning-removal criteria.
The bowl already must be removable and accessible for cleaning. The system-wide sanitation statement adds no change to the bowl removal, swapping, or clearance behavior.
Sanitation access for liquid-contact parts does not alter the platform height, cup clearance, or mixer-fit requirements.
Cleaning and sanitation access does not modify the existing leak-prevention and liquid-containment behavior.
The sanitation-access decision does not change the valve mechanism, button interaction, dispensing sequence, or controlled-flow behavior.
The source decision concerns access for cleaning liquid-contact parts and does not change the spout's geometry, orientation, construction, or pour direction.
The sanitation-access requirement does not require a sourcing-policy exception or otherwise change the simple off-the-shelf V1 approach.
The source does not revise the system-layout or CAD deliverable; the sanitation constraint remains represented by the source Requirement.
The sanitation-access decision does not alter splash-control state. The separate high-RPM splash clause in the message reiterates an already established requirement without adding a new criterion.
Sanitation access for liquid-contact parts does not change the required mixing texture, foam consistency, or high-speed mixing behavior.
